cultural.summary: Early, timely sowing escapes many pests and diseases!
cultural.how: Sow between 10 and 25 October. At Palampur, gobhi sarson sown on 20 October out-yielded 30 October and 10 November sowings.
cultural.evidence: Palampur yield trial (HP); the 10-25 October window and pest-escape advice are from the national NIPHM mustard package.

cultural.summary: The fungus is carried in the seed and on weeds!
cultural.how: Use certified seed, remove weeds (especially related plants), apply the recommended potash, and clear plant debris. Look for concentric brown rings on the lower leaves.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM AESA package (national, not HP-specific). HP average severity 47.1% (AICRP survey, 2004-2020).

cultural.summary: Be realistic: natural options are limited here!
cultural.how: Control rests on timely sowing, clean seed and sanitation. Trichoderma and Pseudomonas gave only 'some' control in a Hisar trial, and the strong results there came from plots that also had a fungicide.
cultural.evidence: Hisar (non-HP) trial; CSK HPKV Kangra extracts gave 65-80% control in pots but their concentrations were not published.

biological.summary: A friendly fungus on the seed!
biological.how: Treat seed with Trichoderma harzianum at 10 g per kg seed before sowing.
biological.evidence: Hisar trial (non-HP); the bio-only benefit was small.

natural_farming.how: Spray jeevamrit diluted to 10% (1 L in 9 L water) in the evening every 14 days, or drench 200 L per acre with irrigation every 15 days.
natural_farming.evidence: ICAR-NEH Meghalaya (non-HP) natural-farming mustard: seed yield 16-44% above control, with no pest or disease data. No natural input had disease-control data on mustard in HP.

details.what_it_does: Builds soil microbial life. Traditionally credited with suppressing fungal and bacterial diseases, but this is not quantified.
materials_needed: A handful of undisturbed bund/forest soil
preparation_steps: Mix all ingredients in a 200 L drum and make up to 200 L with water.
Cover with a cloth or gunny bag and keep in shade.
application_steps: Dilute 1 part strained jeevamrit with 9 parts water (10%) and spray in the evening, or run 200 L per acre into irrigation water every 15 days.
Use soon after it is ready.
safety_notes: Do not apply on waterlogged soil.

cultural.summary: Raised creamy-white pustules, not brown rings!
cultural.how: Look for raised creamy-white pustules on the leaves; in humid weather flowers swell and distort ('stag head'). It is often mixed with downy mildew.

cultural.how: Remove and burn previous crop debris, especially stag heads, avoid over-irrigation and waterlogging, and rotate with non-mustard crops.

cultural.how: Look for grey-white patches on the lower leaf surface and swollen flower stalks. It likes 10-20 C and humidity above 90%.

cultural.summary: A timely irrigation helps the crop outgrow aphids!
cultural.how: Irrigate in the 4th week after sowing and check the tops of plants from December to March; aphid attacks usually start in the 2nd-3rd week of December.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM AESA package (national, not HP-specific). Not HP aphid data.

botanical.summary: Neem oil cut aphids by about three-quarters in a trial!
botanical.how: Spray neem oil at 3% (30 ml per litre of water) with a little soap as emulsifier, covering the flower and pod tops where aphids cluster.
botanical.frequency: At first colonies; repeat after 10 days
botanical.evidence: Hisar trial (non-HP): 76.4% aphid reduction (dimethoate 93.2%). NIPHM lists neem oil 2%; start at 2% on tender plants.

botanical.how: Spray NSKE at 5% (50 ml per litre of water) on the infested shoots.
botanical.frequency: At first colonies; repeat after 10 days
botanical.evidence: Hisar trial (non-HP): 71.4% aphid reduction. A Meghalaya mid-hill trial of 5% plant extracts gave only 50-62%.

cultural.summary: Sawfly larvae attack seedlings in October-November!
cultural.how: Sow before 20 October and irrigate at the seedling stage, since most larvae drown. Look for black-green caterpillars that fall and play dead.
Collect and destroy larvae in the morning and evening, deep plough in summer to destroy pupae, and burn crop residue after threshing.

botanical.summary: A neem spray listed in the national package!
botanical.how: Spray NSKE at 5% (50 ml per litre of water) on the seedlings.
botanical.frequency: At first damage; repeat after 10 days
